references.text: The immediate context: [ref:Luk 12:42-43|Luke 12:42-43] describes the faithful and wise steward whom the Lord puts in charge of his household, and who is found faithful when the Lord returns. Verse 44 is the promise of reward for this faithful servant.

[ref:Matt 24:47|Matthew 24:47] is a direct parallel passage to Luke 12:44 in Matthew's version of the parable: "Truly, I say to you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions." The wording is almost identical.

In the parable of the talents in [ref:Matt 25:21-23|Matthew 25:21-23], the master says to the faithful servants: "You have been faithful over a little; I will set you over much." This is the same principle: faithfulness in stewardship leads to being entrusted with even more.

In the parable of the minas in [ref:Luk 19:17-19|Luke 19:17-19], faithful servants are rewarded with authority over cities. The principle is the same as in 12:44 – faithful stewardship leads to greater responsibility and reward.

[ref:Luk 16:10-12|Luke 16:10-12] expresses the principle that whoever is faithful in little will be entrusted with much. This supports the promise in 12:44 that the faithful steward will be put in charge of all the Lord owns.

[ref:Heb 3:2-6|Hebrews 3:2-6] speaks of Moses, who was faithful in all God's house, and of Christ as Son over God's house. The theme of faithfulness in managing God's household connects to Luke 12:44.

[ref:Åp 2:26|Revelation 2:26] promises that the one who conquers and keeps doing Jesus' works until the end will have authority over the nations. This reflects the eschatological promise that faithfulness is rewarded with authority, as in Luke 12:44.

[ref:1 Tim 3:14-15|1 Timothy 3:14-15] refers to God's household and its management. The idea of being placed over God's household as a faithful steward has parallels to the entrusted servant in Luke 12:44.

[ref:1 Mos 39:4-6|Genesis 39:4-6] tells how Joseph was put in charge of all that Potiphar owned because the Lord was with him. This is an Old Testament foreshadowing of the faithful servant who is entrusted with everything his master owns, as described in Luke 12:44.

[ref:Ordsp 8:21|Proverbs 8:21] says that wisdom gives riches to those who love her and fills their storehouses. The principle that faithfulness and wisdom are rewarded with abundant stewardship reflects the promise in Luke 12:44.
